h1: Metal belt grinders, disc sanders and bench grinders
intro: Belt grinders are the finishing machines of the fabrication shop: they take the burr off a cut, blend a weld, square an end and put a chamfer on an edge faster than a hand grinder and with a flatter result. NovoTech's value-line grinders are built in China to our specification: pedestal belt grinders with 3″ and 6″ belts up to 5.5 HP, a mobile floor grinder for weld seams, wide-belt grinders with 4″ and 8″ belts, knife and tool grinders, combination machines with a belt, a disc and a wheel on one motor, disc sanders to 20″, bench grinders and wire-wheel machines, edge chamfering machines, end-surface grinders and the dust collectors that keep metal dust out of the shop. Parts and belts from Mississauga, ON, Canada.

faq.a: 2″ belts (2 × 72″, 2 × 79″) are for knives, tools and detail work; 3″ is the all-round width for deburring and blending in the fabrication shop; 4″ and 6″ belts grind wider parts flat and last longer; 8″ belts are for flat sanding of wide parts and for radius grinding. Most shops start with a 3″ or 6″ pedestal grinder and add a disc sander for flat faces.

faq.q: What belt speed for steel, stainless and aluminum?
faq.a: Around 5,000 – 6,500 ft/min for steel and stainless with zirconia or ceramic belts; slower — 2,500 – 4,000 ft/min — for aluminum, for heat-sensitive parts and for fine finishing. The two-speed and variable-speed grinders (S-150, SDD75, BGM-50, SP-2) cover both.

A belt grinder removes metal faster, grinds radii on the contact wheel and runs cooler because the belt is long; a disc sander gives a flat face and an accurate angle against its table — chamfers for welding, squaring ends, deburring flat parts. The combination machines (SP-6, BTM250) put both on one stand.

faq.q: Do I need a dust collector for metal grinding?
faq.a: Grinding dust settles everywhere and is a health and housekeeping problem; a collector at the machine keeps it out of the air. Use a collector made for metal — sparks reach the filter — and never connect the same collector to a woodworking machine: wood dust and hot metal sparks are a fire hazard. The DVS14 and DC650 are metal-only collectors; for heavy production the WD-1800 wet collector is on the deburring machines page.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models with a small enough motor. Manual machines have no electrics.
